properties.title: Mg# Magnesium Number · Clementine 1D-CNN (Qiu et al., 2025)
properties.authors: Denggao Qiu, Jianguo Yan, Bin Liu
properties.processing:lineage: Derived from the CNN MgO and CNN FeO maps from the same publication. Mg# = molar Mg / (Mg + Fe) = (MgO/40.30) / (MgO/40.30 + FeO/71.85). Both input maps are 1D CNN inversions of Clementine UVVIS 5-band reflectance, trained on 49 ground-truth points including Chang'E-6. First global Mg# map with full polar coverage beyond 65° latitude.
properties.lri:data_use_note: Mg# (molar Mg/(Mg+Fe)) is the primary indicator of magma differentiation and crustal/mantle lithology. High Mg# (>0.7) indicates primitive, undifferentiated material — mantle-derived dunites, peridotites, or early-crystallized cumulates. Low Mg# (<0.5) indicates evolved, iron-enriched mare basalts. Non-maria Mg# (mean 0.632) is significantly higher than maria (mean 0.494). This is the first Mg# map with full global polar coverage, enabling south polar compositional characterization. Prior Kaguya MI-based maps were limited to 65°N–65°S.
properties.lri:quality_note_short: Mg# (molar Mg/(Mg+Fe)) computed from CNN MgO and FeO maps. Global mean 0.609, mode 0.634. Non-maria mean 0.632 vs. maria mean 0.494. First Mg# map with polar coverage beyond 65°. Inherits uncertainty from both MgO (LOOCV R²=0.755) and FeO (LOOCV R²=0.897) inputs.
properties.lri:quality_note: Mg# (magnesium number, molar Mg/(Mg+Fe)) derived from CNN MgO and CNN FeO maps (Qiu et al. 2025, Communications Earth & Environment). Mg# = (MgO/40.30) / (MgO/40.30 + FeO/71.85). Global mean 0.609, unimodal continuous distribution with mode 0.634. Non-maria mean 0.632, significantly higher than maria mean 0.494 — reflecting the iron enrichment of mare basalts relative to highland anorthosites and early crustal cumulates. The bimodal MgO distribution (modes 5.11 and 10.31 wt%) and the unimodal FeO distribution (mode 5.28 wt%) combine as a ratio to produce the unimodal Mg# distribution. This is the first global Mg# map extending beyond 65° latitude; prior state-of-the-art maps from Kaguya Multiband Imager (MI) were limited to 65°N–65°S. The south polar region Mg# analysis identified 42,762 points with FeO >15 wt% and Mg# <0.60 — consistent with mare basalt chemistry — distributed across 96,214 km² (~6.7% of the south polar region), primarily on basin floors, crater walls, and central peaks. Uncertainty is compounded from both input maps: MgO has LOOCV R²=0.755 (the lowest of the five oxides), and FeO has LOOCV R²=0.897. Absolute Mg# values carry combined uncertainty; spatial patterns and relative contrasts are more reliable than point estimates.
